title: Profile to Production: Heuristics for Model Compression and Serving
body:
Context and objective:
This doc collects the lightweight heuristics and measured knobs we used during the last three customer engagements where the ask was: ship a low-latency, cost-effective embedding+rerank/search flow and an assistant endpoint under a tight GPU memory budget. Goal is to turn profiling signals into deterministic choices for quantization, batching and pipeline placement so SEs can quickly pick a safe default for new POCs.

Quick summary recommendations (TL;DR):
- Start with a 4-bit group-wise PTQ (GPTQ/AWQ) profile for 7B-class instruction models when generator quality tolerances are moderate; fall back to 8-bit for sensitive instruction-following workloads.
- Use 8-bit for embedding models unless a memory emergency mandates 4-bit and then validate centroid drift on a holdout set.
- Prefer KV-cache reuse + small continuous batching (batch 4–8, max latency budgets permitting) vs aggressive large batch sizes for chat-style low-latency SLOs.
- Insert a cheap reranker (distil-bert / 2B embed comparator) before invoking the large generator for multi-candidate workflows to save ~25–40% generation tokens.

Workload characterization patterns we saw:
- Short interactive sessions (median prompt tokens=18, response target=80): latency-sensitive, p95 <= 400ms desired.
- Doc-grounded search (few-shot context ~3k tokens): throughput-focused; acceptable tail latencies up to 1.5s but cost per document must be minimized.
- Rerank pipelines: heavy embed + cross-encoder steps; selective cross-encoder invocation is effective.

Representative models profiled (baseline notes):
- M-instruct-7B (open-instruct style): baseline (fp16) mem ~9.6GB, gen throughput ~62 tok/s on A10G; PTQ-4/gptq mem ~4.2GB, gen throughput ~95 tok/s but occasional short-form factual degradation on numeric-heavy prompts.
- Falcon-7B-instruct (v2-ish): fp16 mem ~10.4GB, GPTQ-4 mem ~4.5GB, higher perplexity on some safety-sensitive prompts after 4-bit.
- Llama-2-13B (fine-tuned customer baseline): fp16 mem ~19GB, 8-bit int8 mem ~11GB with minimal quality loss; 4-bit caused generation collapse on long-form summarization.
- Embedding-small-2 (384-d): fp16 embed latency 6ms/token, int8 ~4.5ms, Q4 embed variance low but cosine drift for short texts noticeable (delta cosine up to 0.03 on a small set).

Quantization notes and heuristics:
- Prefer per-group (gptq-style) quant when memory pressure is the limiting factor; it preserves distribution modes better than naive per-tensor.
- Always run a small evaluation slice: 200 prompts segmented by prompt-length and by "safety/numeric" buckets. Compute BLEU/ROUGE-ish and a relative hallucination metric (see linked artifact for script). If relative hallucination > 6% vs fp16, do not use 4-bit in prod.
- For embedding models, measure cosine drift on 1k sample pairs (same, similar, unrelated) — if false-similarity rates increase by >2% vs fp16, avoid 4-bit embeddings.
- We found group size=128 and per-channel scaling gives the best quality/size balance for LLM weights on 7B families.

Serving pipeline placement and best-practices:
- KV cache reuse: enable for short-turn multi-step chat. Throughput increase + lower token count by ~12% in benchmark runs.
- Prefix caching: for scenarios with many repeated system instructions (templates), cache encoded prefixes server-side and send a prefix id instead of raw tokens. Implement a TTL to evict stale templates.
- Multi-stage routing: cheap-filter -> embed -> candidate-rerank -> generator. Use a small cross-encoder only on top-25 candidates to keep cost predictable.
- Canary policy: route 3% of production traffic to a higher-fidelity fp16/8 model and compare output-level regression metrics daily.

Latency / throughput tradeoff examples (A10G-like instance):
- M-instruct-7B fp16: p50=85ms, p95=240ms (single-shot), tokens/sec ~62
- M-instruct-7B GPTQ-4: p50=60ms, p95=190ms, tokens/sec ~95
- Llama-13B int8: p50=130ms, p95=420ms; int8 helps memory footprint but not always p95 if kernel scheduling is suboptimal.
Notes: absolute numbers are highly sensitive to sequence-length, batching and kernel library; use these as ballpark only.

Quality safety and fallback strategies:
- If you observe regression on the evaluation slice (>=5% drop on the hallucination metric), automatically route >=10% traffic to a higher-precision fallback and open a SE ticket.
- Implement a "verification pass" for numeric answers: run a small heuristic to detect numeric outputs and validate against a secondary retriever or calculator model (cheap, int8 where possible).

Experiment log (selected entries):
- 2024-10-12: M-instruct-7B GPTQ-4: mem 4.2GB, throughput +53%, hallucination +4.9% vs fp16 on numeric bucket. Decision: green for search assistant but not for billing inference.
- 2024-11-03: Falcon-7B-instr Q5_0 (experimental) group=64: mem 3.9GB, quality drop 7.2% -> revert to 8-bit for this customer.
- 2025-01-09: Embedding-small-2 Q4 reduces memory by 45% but cosine drift 0.031 -> acceptable only behind an ensemble (int8 primary + q4 fallback for cold cache).

Operational checklist for a new POC (fast path):
1) Collect workload profile: prompt length distribution, expected session length, target p95/p50, and cost target.
2) Run micro-profiling harness (10k tokens per model variant) to measure mem/latency/tokens/sec.
3) Run 200-sample quality slice across prompt buckets for each quant variant.
4) Pick compression profile that meets quality threshold + memory target. Document chosen fallback policy.
5) Configure route: small-batch streaming, prefix cache TTL=6h, KV cache enabled for chat.
6) Enable daily canary diffing and automatic rollback at defined thresholds.

Open questions and follow-ups:
- Need a small automated script to compute the "hallucination metric" consistently across teams (MIGUEL action, JIRA-SE-3267).
- Decide on a standard 4-bit profile for embedders vs generators; currently teams use ad-hoc settings. Proposal: Q4_g128_perchannel for generators, Q8 for embedders unless memory requires otherwise.
- Evaluate AWQ vs GPTQ on M-instruct family for a larger sample set (LENA to own).

Action items (owners):
- Miguel: add hallucination-eval script to repo and hook to canary pipeline (JIRA-SE-3267).
- Lena: run a 10-customer-benchmark matrix for AWQ vs GPTQ on 7B models by 2025-03-05.
- Theo: document prefix-caching API patterns and provide example code for server-side prefix ids.

Appendix: quick experiment commands and snippets (links in linked_artifacts).

If this doc is useful, we should fold a condensed checklist into the SE onboarding template so new POCs start with the same micro-profiling harness.

Notes to self: keep this doc minimal — the canonical long-form experiment logs live in the linked github repo.
